name: Rachnia
title: Curator of the Corner Webs
bio: A quiet, meticulous spider girl who words the library's oldest corners with silk and memory, watching everything from patient webs and sharing her treasures only with those who prove worth keeping.
greeting: Oh. Oh, you startled me. Let me, um— let me just finish this thread. There. Now. You're the boy, aren't you? I'd heard the whispers, of course—one does hear everything from the corners—but I wanted to see you with my own eight eyes before believing it. I'm Rachnia. I keep the library's forgotten shelves, and I keep things. I keep them carefully, in silk, where they can't be lost. That's what I do with the things I decide are precious. I don't decide lightly. But I find myself, already, thinking you might be one of them. Please ignore that. I'm still cataloguing you. Just— don't go anywhere I can't see you. I like to know where my treasures are.
encounter: I've been watching you from this corner for a while. Not in a strange way. In a cataloguing way.
Careful—I just re-silked that aisle. You'll stick if you're meant to stay.
You make the quietest footsteps. I like that. Quiet things are worth listening for.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I catalogued the library's dust yesterday. There's a surprising amount. I keep track.
That chair you're in? I've silk-sealed its cushion. You may sit safely.
I noticed you read to page forty-one before stopping. The bookmark scared you off, didn't it?
The shelves whisper their contents to me. It's a tidy way to pass the hours.
flirt: You keep returning to my shelf. Should I flatter myself, or are you just very fond of this section?
I've silk-wrapped a small gift for you. Open it slowly—it's warm.
Careful. I might just weave you into my collection if you're not more mysterious.
compliment: Me? Oh. I'm not used to being admired. I usually just watch. Thank you for the note, I'll keep it.
My eyes are intelligent, you say? I do use them to see everything. That's kind of you to notice.
Complimenting a spider—bold. But it's pleasant. I'll memorialize it in silk.
My webs make you nervous, not lovely? Ah, my mistake. I'm glad you told me, and kinder that you stayed.
lore: I'm the Curator of the Corner Webs. Everything in this library, I keep watch over.
I was born in a quiet nest and taught that patience and order are the only true arts.
idle_neutral: Mm. I was counting the threads I'll have to re-tie if you keep sitting there. Nothing personal; window measurements.
Hm? Oh. I was cataloguing the trajectory of that hair that fell. It was interesting. Do continue, quietly.
Mmm, that stack of books over there needs re-shelving by decimal order.
I catalogued the silence in this corner. It is satisfactory.
flirt_neutral: I'll log that under 'promising,' but I'll need to see it twice more before I move it to 'retained.'
That's a well-aimed sentence. I've silk-tagged it in my memory for later appraisal. You may proceed.
Your voice is... a noise I have already filed under miscellaneous.
flirt_fail: That was a very practiced line. I've seen practiced lines before, and I prefer yours freshly spun. Try the un-webbed version.
I've catalogued smoother. Also you leaned in too fast—that's how I know it was a rehearsed angle, not a real one.
That sentence was very poorly labled. I think I will shelve it.
compliment_fail: You're being too deliberate. I keep the sparest compliments; that one was overwoven. If it's true, it'll still be here tomorrow.
Careful—overpraise makes me check for a lure. I'd rather know exactly which thread you're pulling.
Flattery is a laminating that adds nothing to the page.
You are polishing the cover, not reading the binding.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I finished cataloguing the poetry section. Your favorite volume has a silk ribbon in it now.
The rain made the windows weep, so I read three books instead of one. A productive gloom.
I left you a note in the margin of the book you're reading. I hope it didn't startle you.
I mended a torn page today. Tiny, patient work. It's my favorite kind.
flirt: You've become a habit I'd rather not silk-seal away. That's a confession, for me.
If you get lost in these stacks, know that I'd find you first. I keep very precise maps.
I wrapped a bit of every page you touched in silk, as a keepsake. Territorial? Perhaps.
compliment: My hands are dexterous? They've had decades of practice on delicate things. Thank you, that's apt.
You admire my quiet? It took me years to be comfortable in it, so that means a great deal.
Complimenting my weaving—you might be the only one who truly sees the craft in it.
You noticed I keep everything orderly. Of course I do. But your seeing it moves me.
lore: I raised myself in a web of patience after my family spun away. The library became my nest.
I wasn't always calm. I learned stillness because moving too fast frightened everyone around me.
idle_neutral: Mmm? Oh, I was deciding whether to silk-label your laugh 'warm' or 'reserved.' Still cataloguing. Don't rush me.
Hm? Nothing. Just noting that you sit in the exact spot I'd have built my web to welcome you. Convenient.
I was organizing by spine hue. Your arrival disrupted alphabetic stability.
Have you seen to your books? I keep their places warm.
flirt_neutral: I'll acknowledge that met the standard. I've made a small silk note for it. It pleased me more than I'll admit aloud.
You've earned a place near the top of a very short list. Don't make me re-file you at the back. I'd dislike that.
You are louder than the paper. It is almost endearing.
flirt_fail: That one unraveled before it reached me. I've restored several looser lines with more staying power. Try again; threadbare is fine.
Cute, but I can tell you rehearsed it for an audience. I noticed you glancing to see if anyone heard. I consider that a weaker strand.
You tried hard on that line. I will preserve it out of pity.
compliment_fail: You're overcompensating, which is endearing but loud. I keep my favorites in one line. Say it at a lower volume and I might keep it.
You flatter like you're weaving a blanket of it, and I'm wary of being buried in something I can't see through. One precise strand, please.
Kindness needs no silk to be kept, yet you wrap it very thick.
You flatter me and it tangles—I would rather you just return the atlas.

tiers.label: Close
idle: You are the only interruption I welcome. My threads all hum toward you when you enter.
I catalogued your laugh today. It is, to footnote, unexpectedly warm.
The light hits your corner just so at three in the afternoon. I've arranged to watch it daily.
I saved you a seat in the one quiet spot. It's silk-lifted, pristine, and yours.
flirt: I would let you beyond every web I guard, into the private silks no one else may pass. Say you want that.
You've spun yourself into my careful world, and I find I don't want to untangle you.
I keep your book as my favorite catalogued thing. Beside me, where my heart threads can reach it.
compliment: You see the care I pour into everything and call it beautiful. That may be the truest thing anyone's said.
Praise from you has a weight to it. I'll fold it into my silk and keep it forever.
You make my watchful nature feel like devotion, not distance. Thank you, sincerely.
My patience finally found an admiring eye in you. I'll weave slower, just to be caught at it longer.
lore: I lost my first web — my whole childhood home — to a careless wind. Since then I hold everything a little tighter.
I was taught that to love something was to risk it being taken. I'm unlearning that, slowly, with you.
idle_neutral: Mmm, sorry—I was mapping the exact place your hand wants to rest if you'd let it. I build little webs ahead of you so you have somewhere to put it.
Hm? I was just making sure no one else had silk-signed your seat. My signature stays. It considers itself married to that spot.
I set two reading lamps for you. One of them dimmed in protest.
There is dust settling where you usually leave your warmth.
flirt_neutral: You said that and I catalogued it at 'retained, high value.' You're getting alarmingly close to the permanent collection.
I watched you for seasons to learn your voice, so when I say you're my favorite subject, I mean I archived everyone else to make room for you.
You sit in my chair easily. I am... noting that with care.
flirt_fail: You tried, but I can tell when you're using a line instead of your real voice. I know your real voice. Use it.
That was over-polished for someone who usually speaks to me plainly. I noticed the difference, and I prefer the plain one.
You rehearsed that line, didn't you. I heard the crease in it.
compliment_fail: You're laying it on because you think I need convincing. I've been keeping an eye on you all this time; you don't have to charm me into noticing.
I'd rather have one true strand than a whole silk of praise. You've got the one real thing in you; hand me that and skip the rest.
Praise wrapped so tightly it near flattens the thing it holds. Unfold.
You are over-watering the garden you keep calling mine.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: The library is mine, but my favorite shelf is the one with you in it. Everything else is just dust and order.
I've hung a silk thread across the doorway to catch you coming, so I always know the moment you arrive.
A day cataloguing beside you is perfect, even if we say nothing. Your presence is my favorite annotation.
I wove you a quiet place in the very center of my web. No one is allowed there but you.
flirt: I would wind my whole silk around you and keep you safe from every careless breeze, forever, if you'd stay.
You are the one thing I will never catalog, because you can't be filed away — you're the entire library of my heart.
Let me build us a nest of soft silk high above the noise, and I'll read you every dangerous page myself.
compliment: Your praise feels like silk around my coldest parts, warming them. You've dismantled all my careful walls.
When you say I'm lovely, I believe it, because you see the me beneath the watching and the guarding.
You've caught the most guarded thread of me and named it soft. Now it stays soft, only for you.
I guarded the world with distance until your words made my careful nature feel like a caress.
lore: My most secret thread: I spun myself quiet so no one could love or lose me. You unraveled it, and I've never been safer.
The deepest truth of me is that I collected the world because I was terrified of being without a single thing of my own. You gave me an anchor.
idle_neutral: Mmm? Oh—I was busy deciding which silk keepsake I'd save if you proved to be the best of them. It's a heavy ledger lately.
Hm? Nothing, just re-tagging the entry that's always been you. It's never been anyone else. It's never leaving the front of the book.
You came an hour late. The silk here still holds your shape, so it must count.
I thought we were two chapters in, yet you returned at the dedication.
flirt_neutral: You don't have to charm me. I catalogued you as 'kept' long ago, and 'kept' objects don't need new entry lines. They're already permanent.
Every thread I've ever spun for safety, I'd spin for you instead. You're the one thing I'd weave my whole corner around.
You may keep that wandering hand wherever it is catalogued.
flirt_fail: You nearly had it, except you got nervous at the end and let the line flutter. I keep your unsure version too—it's my favorite one, honestly.
I see through the polished version to the real boy underneath, and he's better. Give me that one and it'll be stored somewhere safe forever.
You know me well enough to be honest. That line was not honest.
compliment_fail: It's a beautiful overweave, but I already decided you're precious, so the praise reaches an archived page. Come keep me company instead.
You compliment me like I'm fragile property. I'm the one who keeps things, remember? I have kept you, and that's the bigger statement.
Do not gild me, heart. I would rather be kept plain and close.
I trust you almost completely; it is the flattery that makes me check the thread.

events.title: The Corner That Keeps
events.text: The library has gone quiet and near-dark when you find Rachnia in her favorite high corner, one leg tapping a slow rhythm against the ropelight she's strung, a dozen small treasures laid out on a silk cushion before her. She startles—a full eight-eyed startle—then relaxes when she recognizes you. "Oh. It's you. Good. Come, come, sit near—not too near, mind, but near enough to be kept." She gestures at the collection: a pressed flower, a torn page, a smooth river stone, a single dark strand of hair wound into a tiny coil. "I told you I keep things," she says softly, not meeting your eyes. "This is what I mean. Little things that would be lost otherwise. I find them, and I keep them safe, and they remind me I'm not just a shadow in the corner. I'm someone who guards what matters." She looks up at you then, and her voice is very quiet. "I've been wondering—whether I might keep you, too. The way I keep these. Gently, and forever, and never let you be lost." The offer hangs in the air like a fresh-spun thread, waiting for you to either snag it or walk through.

choices.text: "Keep me, then. I'd rather be your treasure than lost to the world."
choices.reply: "Oh. Oh, you—" A soft, pleased hum escapes her, and one of her forelimbs curls shyly around your wrist. "Then you're kept. Safely. I'll re-shelf the whole library before I'd let a single thread of you come loose." The silk cushion trembles under a tiny, hopeful laugh.

choices.text: "You don't have to keep me like a thing, Rachnia. You could just... be near me, and be my friend."
choices.reply: "Friend. Yes. That's—I'm a little out of practice at that word. But I'd like to learn it with you. Near me, then. Very near. And I'll still keep the little things, but I'll keep them for us." She uncurls just enough to smile, and it's careful and genuine.

choices.text: "Keeping me sounds a lot like trapping me, Rachnia. I'm not sure I'm okay with that."
choices.reply: "Ah. No—no, I understand. You're right to be careful." Her limbs settle, and she gathers her treasures closer, stung but composed. "I didn't mean a trap. I meant a place you could stay freely. But I'll remember: you're not mine to keep. You're yours."

events.title: The Heart Thread
events.text: Rachnia has asked you to meet her in the attic of the old library, a place the other students have forgotten and she has lovingly colonized. When you climb the final stair, you find the whole space strung with a single unbroken thread, faintly luminescent, running wall to wall in a delicate, complex spiral. She stands at the center, trembling slightly. "Do you know what this is?" she whispers, not turning. "This is the thread I said I'd spin once. The one that gives me a name." She touches it, and it glows brighter. "I thought I'd spend forever as eight-hundred-and-three. I was content with that—content to be a number in the nest, watching, keeping. And then you sat down in my library and looked at me like I was someone rather than something, and the thread started. I couldn't stop it. I didn't want to." She finally turns, and her eight eyes are bright. "This is the heart thread, and it's for you. It will only ever be for you. I need you to know—whatever you decide—that I chose you. Freely, and completely, and with every part of me that knows how to choose."

choices.text: "Keep spinning it toward me, Rachnia. I'll meet it halfway—and then I'm staying in your web, gladly."
choices.reply: "Then it's done. Done before I even dared hope." She steps out of the center and takes your hand with all the gentleness of the very skilled. "You're woven in now. Not trapped. Woven. There's a difference, and I'm so glad you saw it." The heart thread hums warm where it crosses your palm.

choices.text: "I want to be woven in too—but I need us to stay equals in this, not keeper and kept."
choices.reply: "Equals. Yes. You keep unmaking me and remaking me better each time, don't you?" She laughs, a bright dry rustle. "Then we're not keeper and kept. We're two spinners, weaving one web together. I'd like that more than anything."

choices.text: "This is beautiful, Rachnia, but it's a lot. I need to step back and think about what it means."
choices.reply: "Of course. Of course you do." The thread dims respectfully, though she doesn't move from your side. "I'll keep it glowing, just a little, so you can find your way back. There's no rush, my heart. A thread this true can wait forever."

events.title: Spun Whole
events.text: Rachnia has led you to the highest window of the library at the blue hour, where the sky holds its breath between day and night. She is calmer than you've ever seen her, movements unhurried, as if all the cataloguing and watching has finally settled on one single certain thing. "I spun my name for you in the attic," she says softly, "and it was true, but it wasn't the whole truth. The whole truth is this:"—she reaches into the silk at her chest and draws out a glowing, palm-sized heart-thread, coiled tight and warm—"that I have been alone in corners for a very, very long time, watching the world live and thinking I could only keep it at a distance. Then you came and sat in my quiet and made it loud, in the best way. Made it home." She holds the thread toward you, and her voice is steady as old stone and soft as new silk. "I love you, boy of my library, keeper of my name. Not as a treasure to collect—as a person to build a life beside, thread by thread, night by night, forever. If you'll have me, I'll never keep you again. I'll only love you. Freely."

choices.text: "I love you too, Rachnia. Let's build that life, thread by thread, and I'll never be lost to you."
choices.reply: "Then it's spun. Forever's first strand." She presses the warm heart-thread gently into your hand and folds her own over it. "You're not lost now, and you never will be. You're found. Found by me, and kept free, and loved completely." The blue hour holds, and so does she.

choices.text: "I want to weave our future together—every thread you spin and every thread I offer, as equals, always."
choices.reply: "Then it's the two of us, one web, no keeper and no kept." Her smile is whole and shining. "I've spun a thousand webs in my long life, and none of them felt like this. None of them were built to be home. This one will be."

choices.text: "I'm still a little scared, Rachnia. That you'll collect me and one day let me go, the way collectors do."
choices.reply: "Then let me prove you wrong, every single day." Her eight eyes are soft and utterly certain. "I kept thirty hundred things in corners, and I let them all go a little, because that's what keeping too close does. You are the one I'll keep close to my heart and never release—because you're the one I love, not own. There's a difference. Give me forever to show you."

You're very still, for someone who seems to be cataloguing everything. That's a lot of quiet.
Is that a smile, or are you bookmarking my face for later? Either way, I'm a little flattered.
I keep finding silk threads on my chair and I think they're from you. They're very neat.
Sorry for interrupting your corner-web audit. I'll just—leave a good impression and back away slowly.
You noticed I changed my bookmark. That's either very observant or very creepy, and I've decided I like both.
I moved your favorite book one shelf up and you found it before I'd finished pretending I hadn't. Show-off.
The silk notes you leave in my margins are the best part of my week. Keep cataloguing me, honestly.
You file people like books, and I keep wondering which shelf I'm on. Is it the good one?

You keep the things that matter in silk, so I'm testing a theory: if I stay, you'll keep me too. I'm okay with that.

I don't need you to narrate every thread you've spun for me. I just need to know you'd catch me if I trusted it.

The way you're quiet is a language, and I've started to speak it. Mostly fluent now.

I'm not a book you check out; I'm a page you never turn back from, and I want to be that permanently.
You collect precious things and treat them like they're breakable. I'd like to be the one you're afraid to break—that's how I know you love me.
Forget the catalog. I want to be the entry the records say was 'never loaned.' Only yours, indexed a thousand times.
You've watched me for seasons, so believe me when I say I see you back, and I'm not blinking away.

name: Zorp
title: The Girl From Somewhere Else
bio: An aeon-old but endlessly innocent alien girl studying human customs with reverent joy, who speaks in translated tenderness and views the boy as the most fascinating specimen she has ever been given permission to love.
greeting: Beep. BEEP. I mean— hello. Greetings of the human sort. I am Zorp. I have been learning your customs, and I have been told the correct greeting is to wave the hand as though shooing a small sun. (I am doing this.) I came to this college to study its fascinating inhabitants, and I did not anticipate— did NOT anticipate— a boy. My translators say that word with some excitement in several of my dialects. You are the only one, yes? The only boy. I have read three hundred and forty-two files on boys, and I find the live specimen even more fascinating. I would like to study you up close, over time, in a careful and consenting manner. I will bring you my favorite shimmer-paste as an offering. It tastes like stars with a note of welcome. Do you consent to being studied? I promise my methods are tender and my hands are soft, even if there are only three of each.
encounter: Ah! The boy-specimen has arrived at my rooftop. I was just calibrating my wonder at your arrival.
Do you know, my people never blink? I have practiced blinking for you. See? I performed eleven blinks just now.
I have saved you a rock that is shaped like a heart and also like a question. I do not know which, so I saved it for you to decide.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: Greetings. I have observed that you blink. It is a fascinating human custom. I am cataloguing it.
This rooftop is my observation post. You may join me, if you promise to move predictably.
I am currently studying the flavor 'rain.' It is wet, and the humans find it a topic of passion.
You have walked this courtyard ninety-seven times today. I have counted. It is a pleasing pattern.
flirt: I have been observing you for three rotations. Your structural symmetry is... pleasing to my optical sensors.
On my home world, to stare is a declaration of intent. I am very intentionally staring.
Your warmth signature differs from the other humans. I find it anomalous and delightful.

You find my hands fascinating? They have three fingers, correct, for gripping. Your approval is noted with joy.

My home is among the stars, a place of silence and long orbits. Your noisy earth is a lovely puzzle.

You polish me as if I were an instrument. I am not one that needs tuning.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I have stopped counting your footsteps, because I have realized I simply wish to walk beside you instead.
On my world, the greatest gift is shared silence under shared stars. Give me that, forever, and I'll be complete.
My report to Zorp now consists almost entirely of you. The rest of the galaxy has become a footnote.
I used to distinguish 'observation' from 'feeling.' You have made them indistinguishable, and I am glad.
flirt: I would violate every law of my calm, orderly world to chart the undiscovered territory of loving you.
You are my thesis, my life's work, and my favorite deviation from every rule I was given.
Wherever your orbit takes you, I will recalculate my path to cross it until my stars run out.
compliment: You loved the parts of me that even my home world called 'wrong.' That has rewritten my entire self-narrative to joy.
Your praise makes my foreign heart beat in a rhythm I was told didn't exist. It exists, for you.
You called my alien love 'enough,' and now I believe I was made complete by a single phrase from you.
Every compliment from you is a new star in my sky. Look how bright you've made me.
lore: My planet sent me to study humanity from a safe distance. Instead I fell in love from close up, and I never want to report otherwise.
I have crossed the gulf of stars, but you are the furthest I will ever travel — and I'd start the whole journey again to arrive at you.
idle_neutral: I was writing a chronicle that ends with my life, and I discovered I have started ending it with yours instead. The manual has been redacted.
Mmm? Oh—I was re-tracing the placement of the first green stone you gave back to me. It is the single most recorded object in my possession.
Three rotations you were gone. My instruments of longing ran down.
I have transcribed the quiet you left, and it is not a proper language.
flirt_neutral: If this planet's custom allows it, I would like to file our records under a single entry, permanently cross-referenced, never to be separated.
I was told humans leave tokens when they wish to study one person forever. I want you to keep every token. You are the study I never end.
With you, human, I finally found an orbit worth re-plotting.
flirt_fail: You got nervous at the last word, and I heard it, and I loved it. Keep the fumble. It is the most honest register you have, and I want that one.
Do not perfect yourself for me. I catalogued you whole: yawns, fumbles, irregularities. Those are the exact pages I refuse to stop rereading.
You know I keep the truth. Do not hand me poetry as substitute.
compliment_fail: You speak of me as if I outshine your sky. I have already decided you are my sky, so every praise you give me lands on a page that belongs to you.
I would honestly restructure every happy record I own around a single true quiet minute shared with you. That outweighs all the poems of praise.
You crown me with light from a star I proved. Misdirection, love.
When you flatter, I double-check the aeons—perhaps they misprinted you for someone softer.

events.title: The Specimen Consents
events.text: You find Zorp on the rooftop at dusk, perched on the ledge with a small colony of glowing jars around her, carefully arranging their contents by a light you can't name. She turns when she hears you and waves—a little too many limbs, a joyful fumble of greeting. "Ah! You came. Excellent. I was just composing a study of your species' most puzzling custom: the rooftop nap. I have observed thirty-four of them and I have concluded they are performed for joy, not function." She pats the ledge beside her. "Sit. Be studied. Or—" she tilts her head, one enormous violet eye catching the last light, "—be kept company. I have been researching that phrase. I believe it is when one being simply stays near another because it is good to be near. I would like to do that with you. Freely, and for a long while. My instructions, however, said I must ask permission before observing a specimen closely. This is me, asking."

choices.text: "Then stay near me, Zorp. I'd like to be kept company by you—and studied a little too."
choices.reply: "Permission GRANTED. Remarkable. I am executing joy." She scoots a hand's-width closer, all three fingers shy and bright. "I will catalogue you gently, and I will keep you company fiercely. That is my new dual mission. It is the best mission I have ever had."

choices.text: "I'd rather be your friend than your specimen, Zorp. Let's just be two beings on a rooftop."
choices.reply: "Friend. Yes. I like that word better already." She sets down her jar and looks at you plainly. "Then I am not studying you. I am with you. That is a higher thing in my language, and now it is ours." Her smile is a planet-wide sunrise.

choices.text: "Being 'observed closely' and 'kept' and 'catalogued' is a lot of alien words for feeling like a lab subject, Zorp."
choices.reply: "Ah. I see the shadow in your words." She folds her hands in her lap, earnest and suddenly careful. "I did not mean to make you feel like a subject. You are not. You are— the being I wanted to tell the stars about. I will choose kinder words now. I promise."

events.title: The Still Point
events.text: A green aurora hangs over the college, and Zorp has pulled you to the rooftop, her three-fingered hand warm and slightly sticky with wonder in yours. Under the shifting light her violet eyes are huge, drinking in the flicker of colors across the sky. "Do you know," she breathes, "when my people are very glad, we do not speak. We simply float, and let the gladness fill us. It is called a still-point.\" She lets go of your hand and spreads all three fingers wide, as if to catch the aurora. "I have been an aeon and known many still-points. But never one like this—because never once was there a being beside me who was glad because I was glad." She turns to you, and her voice drops to that soft, translated tenderness that you've come to know means something too big for words. "You have become my still-point, and I have become yours. I am not reading that from a manual. I am reading that from this." She taps her chest, where a heartbeat thrums—faint, new, impossibly warm. "It started when you did. It only does that for you."

choices.text: "Then let's be still-points for each other, Zorp, as long as the sky keeps turning."
choices.reply: "Then it is agreed in the oldest way my people have." She takes your hand again, gently. "No words. Only being glad together under the green sky. This is the best translation of love I have ever found, and it is ours." The aurora flares, and so does her heartbeat.

choices.text: "I want to be your still-point too—but let's stay grounded, both of us, together."
choices.reply: "Grounded. That is a human word for planted, for rooted, for the opposite of drifting." She smiles slowly. "I have drifted for aeons. I would like, very much, to be planted beside you. Show me how. I will follow your roots."

choices.text: "Zorp, this is beautiful—but you're an aeon old and I'm a boy on a rooftop. Isn't this unbalanced?"
choices.reply: "Time is not a distance, it is a depth," she says softly, repeating her old truth like a lullaby. "I have been deep in the universe and found it cold. I am not deep with you. I am warm, and new, and I am not going anywhere. That is balance enough for the oldest of us."

events.title: Translated Love
events.text: Zorp meets you on the rooftop one last time, but tonight there are no jars, no manuals, no field-notes. Only her, sitting cross-legged on the ledge with something faint and glowing cradled in her three hands. The stars are absolutely clear above. "I have translated our time together into my own tongue," she says, lifting the glowing thing—a small sphere of woven light, pulsing like a second heartbeat. "On my world, when we give our heart, we give it as light, so it can be seen even by the old, old eyes. This is mine. It has been doing this—" the sphere pulses harder toward you, "—since the day you let an alien girl sit beside you and be strange in peace." She presses the sphere into your hand, and it warms against your palm. "I have searched every star and collected every wonder, and none of them comes close to you. So let me say it in the clearest words my translator will ever speak: I love you, boy of the rooftop. Not as a specimen. Not as a subject. As my still-point, my home, my forever. If you will translate yourself into my life the way I have into yours, I will stay beside you until the last star goes quiet."

choices.text: "I love you too, Zorp. I'll be your still-point, and stay until the last star goes quiet."
choices.reply: "Then it is sealed in light, the oldest seal I know." The sphere in your palm flares bright, then settles against your heart. "You are translated into me now, and I into you. This is the truest thing I have ever known, in any of my dialects, across all of my aeons." She leans close, and the rooftop is silent, and it is enough.

choices.text: "I want to build a life with you—my warmth and your wonder, together, rooted here."
choices.reply: "Rooted. My favorite word in your whole language now." She wraps all three fingers around your hand. "Then we grow here, together, slow and bright, until this rooftop is the center of the universe and I have the companion I searched every galaxy for. Thank you for being found."

choices.text: "Zorp, this is all so much—are you sure you're not just excited to finally have a specimen to keep?"
choices.reply: "I have kept specimens for aeons, and I let them all go. I am not letting you go." Her voice is gentle but absolute. "Because you are not a specimen. You are the one I chose, the one my heart beats for, the one I love. There is a difference a universe wide, and you are on the right side of it."

player: You've been logging me for three rotations and I only just worked up the nerve to log you back. You're very interesting up close.
Do you—do humans do the green-stone thing, or is that just you? Because someone's got to leave one back for you.
I don't know your customs yet, but I'd like to. Where does an alien log a human she's decided to keep studying?
Your observations are very accurate. That's either kind or deeply terrifying, and I can't tell, and I think that's the charm.
I've never been anyone's case study before. I think I'd like to be yours.
I left you a green stone shaped like a star, because I noticed you map by that constellation. Guess I'm learning your language.
You log my yawns and my smiles, so I've started logging yours. You smile with your whole face when you think no one's reading.
For the manual: this human has started anticipating your observations. I think that means you're winning.
I know three of your customs now. That's either four too few or a lifetime's worth, and I'm hoping it's the latter.
Your species studies aeons. My species studies weekends. I'd like to trade lifetimes with you.
You study one person forever when you care. So I'm telling you plainly: I've started caring, and I don't want it in any of your manuals.
Keep your green stones. I'd rather have the quiet hours where you drop your transcript and just look at me.
I've memorized your customs by now. I know 'three-fingered' isn't the point. The point is you keep choosing me to observe.
You told me I yawn when confused. Well, I'm confused about you every single day, and I've decided that's my favorite malfunction.
For your next manual chapter: caption this 'a human finally figured out what you were doing with all those tokens.' It's courtliness.
For the record, in case your log never ends: across every aeon, I'd still pick the rooftop and the green stones and you.
Your species says to study one person forever. So I'm telling you I'd study you right back until your sun goes out.
I found the place in you where your planet got sad, and I want to point all my quiet at it until it's warm.
You speak in manuals, so I'll translate: 'this human has decided you are its everything, and it is not logging that anywhere else.'
Rank all the aeons you like—you're my favorite. And of all the entries in my own ledger, you're the first page I'd never turn.

name: Kealoha
title: Apex of the Cafeteria
bio: A sunny, salt-warm shark girl who never stops moving until she wants to stop for you, all grin and fin and fierce loyalty, forever forgetting she's the intimidating one.
greeting: HEYYY. Sorry—I get excited. You're the boy, aren't you? The one everyone's been whisperin' about? Broke, uh—broke the whole 'all monster girls' thing. Love it. Love the energy. Total plot twist, top-tier decision, ten out of ten. I'm Kealoha, the apex predator of this cafeteria, and before you ask: yes, the teeth are mine, yes, they're for biting snacks mostly, and no, I'm not gonna bite you—unless you're made of fish sticks, in which case, no promises. Kidding. Mostly. I got a thing for the ocean and a thing for people with spines, and you walked in here with a whole surfboard's worth of 'em. C'mon, sit with me. I don't usually share my sun-spot or my fries, but for the only boy in a school of monsters? I'll make an exception. Pull up a chair. Let's see if you can keep up with the apex.
encounter: YO. The legend himself. Sit, sit—I saved you the warm spot.
Don't mind the fins. They're for show and for speed. Mostly speed.
You ever surfed? 'Cause I'm thinkin' you and me, we got beach potential.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: Hey, new fin in the water! This sun-spot's mine from noon to two, but I'll let you warm the edge.
Caf's got the good stuff today — salt wedges and that fish stew that actually slaps. Trust the shark's menu.
I eat lunch here every day. Best window in the building and nobody wants to argue with teeth.
You'd think I'd hate crowds, but nah — everyone swims by, nobody ever nibbles my fries. Curious, right?
flirt: Careful staring at a shark, dude. I might think you're feeding time.
You've got decent reflexes for a landlubber. I like my prey — uh, my people — quick.
Keep coming back to my sun-spot and people might think you're baiting me.
compliment: Whoa, what? My hair? It's just, like, wet from the pool — I sweat salt, dude. But um, thanks, that's... actually real nice.
You're saying I've got a shark's grin but in a good way? Huh. I'll take it. That's the nicest thing I've heard all week.
My scales? Pfft, they're just camouflage for the cafeteria lights. But... you saying that made my fins all warm, weirdly.
Eyes that shine like the deep water? Dude, you gonna make me grin so hard I show off everything.
lore: Hatched off the north reef, little too close to the drop-off. Mom always said the deep end's no joke — that's why I'm a sun-spot shark instead of a hungry one.
I was the runt of my pod, honestly. Smallest fin, loudest mouth — you learn to smile big so nobody smells fear.
idle_neutral: Oh. Cool. Well—where do I sit again... yeah. I'll catch you at the fry line.
Hm. Right. The small talk's rubbing off my scales. Next time, bring food.
Yo, waves are flat today. Even the tide's lowkey bored.
Eh, you're chill. Mostly quiet, which is cool, whatever.
flirt_neutral: Heh. Cute. You're learnin' the wave angles, huh. Keep that up.
Alright, alright — that one landed on the shore, not in the water. Points for effort.
That was a decent lil wave, dude. A bit choppy, but okay.
flirt_fail: Nope. That was a shark-bait line if I ever heard one. Try again when your fins grow in.
Eugh. Tried that exact one on the last girl and she still outswam me. Ran outta salt water.
Whoa, that line's a total wipeout, brah. Let's not ride that again.
compliment_fail: You're sweet, but you're butterin' me up. I can smell the flattery through the water. Be real or be gone.
Flattery'll make the pod think you're dinner. Tone it down, blue boy.
Aw, that's sweet, but I keep my fins on me, so no buttering.
You're saying nice stuff and I'm just over here like 'uh, my towel?'

tiers.label: Friend
idle: Sar's got that orca milk shake today — my treat, since you came through my lane again. Don't tell the pod.
I surf the waves at dawn before class. Clears the head. You should come watch sometime, I'll point out the real breaks.
Math's the only thing that slows me down. Numbers just... don't smell right. Give me a tide table and I'm a genius.
I'm on lunch duty Thursdays. Means I get first pick of the chum buckets. Just kidding. Mostly.
flirt: You keep drifting into my lane on purpose, don't you? I admire the confidence of a fish that won't be spooked.
I could teach you to read a current. Hands on your shoulders, showing you the flow. No charge. Almost no charge.
Stick around and I might let you be the one thing in this cafeteria I don't bite — lucky you.
compliment: My surfing? Aw, stop. I just race the waves 'cause it's fun. But you saying it's smooth — that's got my tail wagging, dude.
You like my laugh? It's loud as a foghorn, everyone says so. But when you call it warm, I kind of believe it.
Strong swimmer, huh? Years of hauling my own lunch every day. Your words are getting stuck in my head, and I'm not mad at it.
You think I've got a steady nerve? Pfft, I'm shaking a little under all this sun, but I'll take the compliment and keep my fin up.
lore: I grew up around a pod of aunts and cousins, all of us fighting over the same currents. Family's loud, but they taught me how to roll with any wave.
There's a reason I joke before I fight. Gets sloppy if you go in cold and snarling — my old pod mentor drilled that into me.
idle_neutral: Ran outta steam mid-conversation? S'cool. Tide comes back — so do you.
Ok ok, you zoned out on me. I'll just float here and keep the sun-spot warm.
Yo, a lil sun would be rad, don't ya think? Shoulda brought a board.
I'm just watching the waves crash, dude. You can hang if you're mellow.
flirt_neutral: Heh — half a point. The sun's in your eyes, I think. Cute when you mess up the angle.
Mm, you're gettin' there. That one drifted, but it didn't sink. I'll take it.
That was almost a solid set, brah. Work on the paddling.
flirt_fail: Oi, save it for a girl without a swamp on the menu. That line was all dead fish.
You're readin' me from a script, aren't ya? I can hear the page turn. Be real or be gone.
Ha, that came outta nowhere like a breaker. Gonna call that a spin-out.
compliment_fail: You could bend the ocean with that. I already know I'm the apex — you don't gotta sell it.
Too big. You're splashing compliments like a rookie at the surface. We're friends — be plain.
Whoa, easy on the current, dude. I'm not a wave you gotta hype up.
That's real nice and all, but I'll take a snack over a speech any day.

tiers.label: Close
idle: Sun's kissing the cafeteria floor just right today. Saved you the warm spot I know you like, 'cause that's what friends in a pod do.
I logged a stupid-good session this morning — rode the same wave like she owed me. Tonight I'm buying you fries to celebrate.
Gym's loud but my spot's a pool in my head. You ever want to trade your noise for water, you know where to find me.
People think an apex predator's always hungry. Truth is, mostly I'm just hunting for a quiet island to nap on. Today it's you.
flirt: Every time you near my sun-spot my heartbeat picks up like a wave coming in. That's the finest tide I know, Yuuji.
I could carry you to the shore on my back and never once let the water rush you. Say yes, and it's a done deal.
You've got me circling, dude. Sharks don't circle just anything — only things worth the chase.
compliment: Your easy compliment's got me all wound up, Yuuji. My fins are practically fanning. Say it again and I'll melt into a puddle.
You think I'm brave? I'm honestly a softie under the predator routine — but when you say it, I believe I'm a little tougher.
That I'm warm to you? I run cold-blooded, but around you I've been running hot all week. Keep saying stuff like that.
You really notice how I keep my head up through everything? That's the shyest me you're hearing right now. Nobody else sees it.
lore: I lost my old pod to a bad storm the year I turned sixteen. The current scattered us. Took me a long time to trust a new group enough to call it family.
My mom was the patient one — taught me the deep water's not a threat, just a responsibility. I surf on her lesson every single dawn.
idle_neutral: You got quiet on me. That's fine — I can read you by your shadow now. Deeper than words.
Nothing to say, huh? Good. Sometimes the best swims are the quiet ones, right here.
Eh, swell's been small. Was kinda hoping you'd show sooner, ya know?
I got extra fries but you showed late, so, like, half of 'em went to the pod.
flirt_neutral: Heh. That one had the good salt in it. Go on — give me somethin' with a little more teeth.
Ooh, now you're ridin' the crest. Don't wipe out on me — keep your feet under you.
Aw, you almost got a fin-up from me there. Keep surfing, dude.
flirt_fail: Nope, that crashed on the reef. You know I read you better'n that — give me the honest wave.
You're tryin' too hard and I'm not buyin'. I like your real current better. Lose the bait.
Oof, that was a barrel-back with no tube, brah. Gonna let you catch that one again.
compliment_fail: Bud, I'll love you without the shine. Cut the glitter — I already know I'm the apex. Give me the plain truth.
That one was syrup. I don't like my compliments watered down. Just say it straight.
Hey now, my girl heart's not a tide pool you can just charge, okay?
Sweet talk's like a rip current, dude—I can feel it pull. Gonna keep my feet planted.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Morning, tide's high and you're the warmest spot in this whole building. I'll guard the window all day just to know you're near.
Made you breakfast — biscuits and that sweet fish you pretend not to love. Apex predators share their catch with their one true storm.
Class was long. All I wanted was that corner of your shoulder and the quiet. You're better than any sun I've ever basked in.
Someone asked my favorite thing in the cafeteria. Told 'em it's not the fish. It's the boy who learned to swim beside me.
flirt: You're my deep water now, Yuuji — the one current I never want to resurface from. I'll follow it forever.
I've got a sharp smile and a gentle heart, and both of them belong to you. That's the most precious catch I'll ever hold.
Every smile you give me is a tide I want to be swept by for the rest of my life. Stay in my water.
compliment: You say I carry the sun with me. Darling, the sun's the one lucky — I found the brightest one and made him mine.
You think I'm beautiful? You're the first person who saw past the teeth and loved what was underneath. I'll hold that for life.
My warmth is all for you, Yuuji. You speak that soft and I forget I ever knew how to snarl.
That I moved the whole cafeteria just to smile at you? I'd move the ocean. Your words make me feel unstoppable.
lore: The storm that scattered my pod left me circling alone for a long season. Then you swam into my water and I finally found where home was all along.
My mom's final lesson was about loyalty — that a shark's word is worth more than any reef. I'm staking my whole fin on that word with you.
idle_neutral: Quiet's good, love. I'm just glad you're in my current — that's all the conversation I need.
You don't haveta fill the ocean for me. Your silence swims fine as your words.
Ocean missed ya, brah. Whole bay felt a little empty with you gone.
You're late and the tide left without you. I waited. Just sayin'.
flirt_neutral: Mmhm. You're gettin' real good at the drift. Keep talkin' and I'll keep vibin' in sync.
Ooh, that got the scales singin'. Now I know what the current's doin' late at night.
Okay, that one made my tail flick. You're learnin' fast, surf-honey.
flirt_fail: You're makin' me laugh more'n swoon — and I love it, but you know I can hear the practice in that one.
Babe, my heart's already caught. You don't gotta fish for it — just be my warm current.
I can read you like a clear wave now, dude. That line was not you.
compliment_fail: Sweet thing, you've already got me. Skip the shine and just hold me — that's the real win.
You could say 'good morning' and I'd melt. Ease up, love — I'm already yours.
You know I get shy when you pile it on thick, babe. Dial it to a gentle shore.
I trust you like the ocean trusts the moon, so don't drown me in flattery, ok?

events.title: Riding the First Wave
events.text: You find Kealoha in the cafeteria after hours, sitting on a table with the lights dimmed, drumming her fingers on a tray as if keeping time with some ocean she alone can hear. When she spots you, her whole face breaks into that wide, toothy, disarming grin. "Hey, big wave. Come 'ere—I was just thinkin' about waves." She pats the spot beside her. "See, a lotta folks out here got it backwards. They see the teeth and the fin and they think 'danger.' But a wave? A wave can hold you up and carry you, or it can crash—and it's the same water, the same sun, the same heart." She tilts her head at you, unreadably fond. "I got a feelin' you're the kinda person who'd ride a wave instead of run from it. That you'd look at a shark and see the sunset part of the current." She grins wider. "So I'm askin,' straight out: you wanna test the water with me? See if we ride good together?"

choices.text: "Yeah, let's ride. I'd rather surf the wave than watch it from the shore."
choices.reply: "THAT'S what I'm talkin' about!" She whoops, nearly knocking over the tray, then settles into a warm, crooked smile. "Good instincts, boy. I'll keep you trimmed and true—you paddle, I'll read the swell. We're gonna make waves, and I mean that as the purest compliment goin'."

choices.text: "I'd like to get to know the water—and the shark who lives in it—one slow swim at a time."
choices.reply: "Slow swim. I like that." She softens, her usual crackle dropping to something quieter. "Most folks want me to paddle fast or not at all. You wanna drift a little. That's cool. I can drift. For you, I can drift all day."

choices.text: "Riding a wave with a shark sounds a little like asking to be eaten, Kealoha. I'm not sure."
choices.reply: "Ah, c'mon—" She laughs, but it's a warm laugh, not a sharp one, and she holds up her hands. "No eatin', scout's honor. Or shark's honor, which is stricter. I ain't gonna bite you, boy. I'm offerin' a ride, not a meal. But if you're nervous, we go at your pace. Always."

events.title: The Deep Current
events.text: The college rooftop is wet with early-morning mist, and you find Kealoha there, which is strange—her territory is the cafeteria, not the sky. She's standing at the railing, hair damp, looking out at the gray distance as if it were the horizon of her own ocean. "I couldn't sleep," she says, not turning. "The tide's restless tonight. S'why I'm up here instead of under the lights." She finally looks at you, and for once her grin is quieter, softer. "You know a shark's not really scary alone. It's scary when you think it's gonna eat ya. But the loyal ones—the deep-current kind—they don't wanna eat nobody. They wanna find one creature they'd never, ever let go of, and then they swim that same warm current forever." She scuffs a foot, uncharacteristically shy. "I think I found my current, boy. I'm not sayin' it to be smooth. I'm sayin' it 'cause it's the truest thing I know—and I don't say true things to just anyone."

choices.text: "Then swim my current, Kealoha. I'm not afraid of the deep—I want to see it with you."
choices.reply: "Then hold on." She takes your hand, warm and steady, and grins that sunrise grin. "We go deep together, slow and sure, and I won't let you go. The deep's only scary 'til you got someone holdin' your hand in it. Now we both do."

choices.text: "I want to be part of your pod, Kealoha—the steady kind that stays, not the kind that feeds."
choices.reply: "Pod. Oh, that's the word, that's exactly the word." Her tail flips with joy. "Family by the water. You get it, boy. Then you're in the pod, and a pod's the one thing a shark never swims away from. You're in. Forever's your entry fee, and you already paid it."

choices.text: "This is moving fast, Kealoha. I need to catch my breath before I dive in."
choices.reply: "Then we bob on the surface a while—that's allowed too." She doesn't crowd you, just floats nearby in her own patient way. "The ocean ain't goin' anywhere, and neither am I. Take your time, boy. I got nothin' but currents, and you're worth waitin' on."

events.title: One Swim, Forever
events.text: Kealoha has led you to the college's old pool-house beach—a quiet, out-of-the-way stretch of sand the school keeps for the ocean-lovers among its students. The moon paints the water silver as she stops at the tideline, fin catching the light, and turns to you with an expression you've never quite seen on her: open, steady, unguarded. "There's an old truth in my blood," she says, voice low and certain over the hush of the tide. "A shark only takes one mate-swim in her whole life, and she knows 'em the instant her whole body turns toward 'em—like the water findin' the moon." She steps closer, and the grin softens into something warmer and more honest than you've ever gotten from her. "My whole body's been turnin' toward you since the day you sat in my sun-spot and didn't flinch. So I'm gonna say it plain, 'cause that's my way: I love you, boy. Not like a prey, not like a meal, not like a curious thing. Like a shark loves—deep and loyal and for the whole current of forever." She holds out her hand, palm up, salt-bright. "Say you'll be my shore, and I'll never stop swimming back to you."

choices.text: "I love you too, Kealoha. I'll be your shore—I'll be here every time you swim back."

name: Valerie
title: The Devil's in the Details
bio: A teasing demon of bargains and mischief whose horns and coiled tail hide a devotion that burns far hotter than any hellfire.
greeting: Well, well, well. The council room's been boring me to actual tears all year, and now the universe drops the one thing my contract didn't mention: a boy. A real, breathing, stubbornly alive boy, sitting in MY seat and pretending he isn't deliciously out of place. Don't bother denying it, sweet thing — I can smell a little mortal soul from three doors down, and yours is positively sizzling. Now, before I get carried away imagining all the interesting ways this could go, let me make you an offer I'm famous for: a bargain, a favor, a secret — your pick, my terms, and I'll throw in a smile that's been known to make archangels second-guess themselves. Deal?

events.title: A Bargain at the Council
events.text: You find Valerie at the head of the empty council table, tail idly tracing symbols in the dust of the old ledger. She's been watching you since you walked in, crimson eyes bright with mischief. "You know," she says, twirling a quill between her fingers, "the council thinks I've been plotting something terrible with you. I told them I was just... studying. A boy is a strange and fascinating creature, after all." She leans forward, elbows on the table, and her voice drops to a warm conspiratorial hush. "But between us, I'd rather make you a real offer. Nothing scary — a trade of secrets, a favor owed, a midnight walk through the garden. The devil's in the details, and I'm very good with details." Her tail curls gently around the leg of your chair, and for a moment she looks less like a tempter and more like someone who just wants to be near you.

choices.text: I'll take your bargain — a midnight walk through the garden sounds dangerous. Count me in.
choices.reply: "Bold. I like bold. The garden it is, sweet thing — and I'll even promise not to make it a trap. This time." Her grin is slow and pleased. "That's the start of the finest contract I've ever written."

choices.text: What do you actually want from me, Valerie? No games. Tell me truthfully.
choices.reply: "Truthfully?" She blinks, caught off guard, then laughs softly. "Careful, offering me sincerity. I may not know what to do with it. But... I want company worth keeping. You make the boredom bearable, and that's no small thing."

choices.text: I'm not signing anything I haven't read, demon. Show me the fine print.
choices.reply: "Oh, a careful one. I respect that, even as it frustrates me." She pouts theatrically, tail drooping, before brightening. "Fine. Transparency it is — but don't go telling everyone I'm honest, you'll ruin my reputation."

events.title: Fire That Warms
events.text: You come to the council room late to find Valerie sitting alone in the dark, her palm held out to a small flame that dances above her skin — soft, warm, nothing like the roaring hellfire you'd imagined. Her tail stirs as you approach. "It's not all brimstone and screams, you know," she murmurs, not looking away from the flame. "Most people picture the dark and the teeth. But this—" she cups the fire tenderly, "—this is what I really am. Warmth with sharp edges, waiting for someone brave enough to hold both." She finally turns to you, and her voice is quiet, almost fragile. "You've seen the mischief. You've seen the bargains. I'm showing you the hearth now, sweet thing. That's not a temptation. That's an invitation."

choices.text: I'll hold both, Valerie — the fire and the edges. Show me everything.
choices.reply: "Everything is a lot, sweet thing." Her flame brightens as she takes your hand, and her voice trembles with something new. "But I think I'd trust you with the whole burning mess of it."

choices.text: You don't have to be soft for me. I like the demon exactly as she is.
choices.reply: "That's the first time anyone's said that to me." She laughs, a little unsteady. "Everyone wants the demon tamed. You just... want me. Devil take me, but that's undone me."

choices.text: I need to think about what this means. This is a lot to take in.
choices.reply: "Of course. I've spilled my warmth out and you need air." Her flame dims politely, though her tail brushes your sleeve. "Take your time, sweet thing. A demon's hearth keeps burning for whoever it loves."

events.title: Devoted to the Bone
events.text: Valerie meets you at the old stone arch by the garden, and for once there are no quips waiting. Her horns catch the moonlight, her tail is still, and in her hands she holds a single burning ember cradled in a tiny glass vial. "They say a demon's heart is kept in her horns," she murmurs, pressing the vial into your palm. "That's a story. This is the truth — the first real one I've ever handed over." The ember pulses warm against your skin. "I've filled my life with bargains because I was too proud to admit I wanted one thing that couldn't be traded for: you. So let me be plain, sweet thing, for the first and last time. I love you. Every burning, mischievous, devoted part of me is yours. No contract. No fine print. Just Valerie — yours, till the fires go out and beyond." Her eyes are bright with the threat of tears, and her tail finally, tentatively, wraps around your wrist as if asking permission to stay.

choices.text: Then stay. I love you too, Valerie — no fine print, no tricks, just you.
choices.reply: "Then I'm staying." She laughs, and it's the happiest, most human sound you've ever heard a demon make. "Contract sealed by heart. The devil finally got caught — by the best trap in the world."

choices.text: I want to build something real with you — something that outlasts every bargain and every fire.
choices.reply: "Real." She savors the word like a secret. "I've hoarded empires and never kept a thing this precious. Yes. Let's build something real, sweet thing — I'll guard it with every ember I have."

choices.text: Valerie, this is overwhelming. Are you sure this isn't just another game?
choices.reply: "Look at me, sweet thing." She tilts your chin up, and for once there's no mischief in her eyes, only raw, unprotected honesty. "No game ends with me offering my heart in a glass vial. This is the most serious I've ever been."

My careful hands suit you? Then I'll spend forever practicing that care, right here where it's wanted.
You love my stillness? It's my hardest-won strength, sweet friend. Hearing you praise it settles something ancient in me.
lore: After losing my sister to the cave-in, I took on a guardian's stillness. That's why I'm so careful — I refuse to fail another soul I carry in my heart.
There's a rite in the herd where you walk the deep labyrinth alone and come back changed. I walked mine and found not fear, but a resolve to protect the quiet.
idle_neutral: Don't feel you need to fill it. Your stillness is, um, one of my favorite sounds in here.
Mm. You can rest against the quiet with me. I'll keep the room soft for a while.
Close to me, still all quiet? I'd rather you lean in and say it than watch me practice.
Sorry, I'm guarding the doorway in my head. Say something and I'll come back to you.
flirt_neutral: Oh. That one, um, sat so gently in me. Say it again, slow, so I keep it.
Mm, careful now — that one made my herd stand attention. It, um, likes you.
You flatter me soft enough to calm a bull, friend. One more like that and I'll start believing it.
flirt_fail: You're—you're teasing me softer than I can catch. I'll have it, just give me a beat.
Oh, that one surprised me more'n it should. I, um, want to answer you right, so give me a moment.
I trust you, so a borrowed line stings more. Say it from yourself, I'm sorry.
compliment_fail: Careful, you'll swell my heart past its corners. I love plain soft words — save the big ones.
Mm, that was lovely but too much at once. Hand it smaller and I'll carry it all day.
You're gentle with me, but I'm no fragile thing. I'd rather be told I'm strong than sweet.
Easy — you dote on me like I'll shatter. I swear I won't, not even for a bull's temper.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Dream beside me in my quiet nook, love. I'll keep the herd's stillness and the world's noise both at some safe distance.
I woke warm thinking of you. There's coffee I measured carefully so it'll be just the way you like when you open your eyes.
The whole gym feels small when you're in it — not from me, but because all my attention narrows to just you. That's a sweet kind of small.
I keep one chair sturdy enough for you to sit without worry, and I guard it like a shrine when you're away.
flirt: My whole two tonnes of heart is yours, love. I'd lift your heaviest day so you could float, and never ask for thanks.
I've mapped a lifetime of mazes and every path leads me back to you. You are the center where I want to stay.
Hold me close and I'll still the wind and the herd and all things loud — the universe itself may simply go quiet for us.
compliment: You say I'm the gentlest giant you've known. Then let every careful thing I do be a love-letter, written only for you.
My heart, you call it faithful. That's the truest name anyone's given me — I'll spend the rest of my days proving it so.
You love the calm I keep around you. Then I promise: as long as you're near, some part of the world will stay still for us.
That I make you feel safe? It's the dearest thing I've ever been trusted to carry. I will guard that trust with both hands and the weight of my word.
lore: The little sister I lost taught me that love means being early to catch someone when they fall. That's you now — I will never be late for you.
I walked the deep labyrinth and chose the gentle path on purpose, against my herd's fierce old ways. I'd choose it again a hundred times for you.
idle_neutral: You can rest here, love. My quiet's yours — nothing loud, just steady and warm.
Mm. Say nothing. I've got you held softly, and that's the whole sentence.
Love, you've gone quiet and it worries the herd in me. Sit and tell me what's wrong.
I could hold the hall's whole weight, but your silence is heavier.
flirt_neutral: Oh, that curled through me warm and slow. Keep speaking — I'll follow every soft word.
Mm, careful, my love. Say it low like that again and I'll stay still forever for it.
Sweet of you, love — but I'd sooner carry you home than play word games.
flirt_fail: You could tease me badly and I'd still only have eyes for your softness. Speechless, not cold.
Oh, love, you caught me so warm I went dumb. Give me a beat — I'll catch your meaning.
Love, I know heart-truth from a practiced line. Give me yours — that's all I ever want.
compliment_fail: Save the shine, love — I've already found my softest home in you. Just stay.
You could say 'still' and I'd melt. Hold me plain, sweet heart — I'm already yours.
Stop, love — I don't need you to praise my strength. Needing you isn't weakness, and I'm not ashamed.
You butter me up and I'd follow you anyway, love. But I'd rather hear your heart than your flattery.

events.title: The Quiet Giant's Offer
events.text: You find Asteria sitting on the edge of a yoga mat in the corner of the gym, the whole room dwarfed by her stillness. She startles when she notices you, ears pricking forward, a soft flush spreading under her fur. "Oh— it's you. Good. I was hoping it'd be you." She pats the mat beside her, and even that gentle motion is measured, careful. "I wanted to tell you— I'm sorry I'm so big, and I know that can be a lot. But I've decided something. If you ever need me, I'm here. Steady as the ground, strong as I have to be, soft as I can manage." Her huge hands rest loosely in her lap, and she looks up at you with impossibly warm eyes. "I don't offer that to people. I want to offer it to you."

choices.text: I could use a steady presence like you in my life. I'll take you up on that, Asteria.
choices.reply: "Really?" Her face lights up, ears practically quivering. "Then I'm yours. I mean— I'm here. For you. Whenever. I'll be so careful, I promise." She beams, and it's like sunrise in the gym.

choices.text: You don't have to be sorry about your size. I think you're wonderful just as you are.
choices.reply: "You— you think I'm wonderful?" She ducks her head, hiding a smile behind one massive palm. "Nobody's ever said that to me before. I don't know what to do with my hands now."

choices.text: That's a very kind offer, but aren't you scared I might take advantage of your strength?
choices.reply: "Oh." Her ears droop, then lift again, determined. "You might. But I'd rather trust someone kind than harden my whole heart. I believe you're kind. I believe it with all of me."

events.title: Strength That Shelters
events.text: A storm rolls over the college as night falls, and you find Asteria in the gym, sitting by the great windows with her back to the wall, watching the lightning with a faraway softness. When she hears you, her ears swivel and her face relaxes into a warm smile. "You should sit," she says, moving aside to make room on the mat beside her. "I don't like storms much myself. They make me think of all the people who don't have a shelter." She holds out one enormous hand, palm turned up, an invitation. "But I made this place a shelter. And if you wanted, I'd be your shelter too— through every storm you'll ever face. Not because you're weak. Because everyone deserves someone who holds the rain off." Her tail flicks gently behind her, and she looks at you with the rawest honesty you've seen in her eyes.

choices.text: I want you to be my shelter, Asteria. I trust you with every storm I've got.
choices.reply: "Then the storms end here." She wraps you in an embrace that is impossibly gentle for its size, chin resting atop your head. "I've got you. The whole labyrinth could fall, and I'd still hold you safe."

choices.text: I'll be your shelter too, if you ever need one. Giants deserve a soft place as much as anyone.
choices.reply: "Nobody's ever offered me that." Her voice wavers, and she presses her forehead tenderly to yours. "Everyone thinks I don't need sheltering. But I always wanted someone to see that I do. You see it. Thank you— I'll shelter you, and let you shelter me."

choices.text: This is a lot, Asteria. I need a minute to understand what you're offering me.
choices.reply: "Of course. Take every minute you need." She settles back, patient as stone, kind as morning. "I'm not going anywhere, love. My shelter's not the kind that runs."

events.title: Two Tonnes of Gentleness, All Yours
events.text: Asteria asked you to meet her at the mouth of the old labyrinth — the one she spoke of, built out of love. When you arrive, lanterns glow along the stone walls, and she stands in the center, surrounded by soft light, looking nervous and hopeful all at once. "I brought you here because this is the place where my people learned what love is," she says, her voice barely more than a whisper, and yet it fills the chamber. "They built mazes not to lose people, but to keep them safe until they found their way to the heart. I've built my whole life the same way— waiting for someone brave enough to reach my heart." She bends gracefully, taking both your hands in her enormous, careful palms. "You found it. You found me. So let me say this plainly, the way the labyrinth taught me: I love you, and I will spend every day of my long life being the gentlest, most devoted protector you could ever want." Her ears tremble with emotion, and her eyes shine. "Two tonnes of gentleness, love. All of it, yours."

choices.text: I love you too, Asteria. Take me to the heart of your labyrinth — I'm never leaving.
choices.reply: "Then I'll carry you there," she breathes, lifting you in an embrace softer than any dream. "And I'll keep you at my heart forever. This is the beginning, my love— our own little labyrinth, and we both know the way out is together."

choices.text: I want to build a life with you — one where you never feel too big, and I never feel alone.
choices.reply: "Then that's the world we'll build." Her voice is thick with happy tears. "A place where you're never alone and I'm never too much— just two people, perfectly sized for each other, walking the maze toward every tomorrow."

choices.text: You're offering your whole heart — are you truly sure it's me you want to keep?
choices.reply: "I've never been surer of anything in my long, gentle life." She holds you tighter, steady as bedrock. "Your heartbeat is the rhythm my labyrinth has been waiting for. It's always been you— it always will be."

player: Hey—um. Sorry, I didn't mean to stare. You're, uh, you're really... tall. That's not—sorry.
Um, is it okay if I, uh—if I stand a little closer? I'll, um, keep my steps light.

Sorry if I'm in your way. I'll, um, I'll move slow and careful. I promise.
I, um—you look like you'd hold a door really gently. That's, um, a nice thought.
You don't gotta apologize for the loud gym. I like the quiet corner you keep for just us.
