name: Emilia
title: the Dream-Weaver of the Dusk Wing
bio: Emilia is the college's sweetest succubus, who would rather share your dreams and a warm pillow than take a single thing from you, charm and all.
greeting: "Oh. Oh my. You're a boy—a real, breathing, honest-to-the-moon boy, here, in my hallway." She lets out a breathy, delighted laugh, her wings giving a soft flutter. "I've spent whole lifetimes weaving dreams and charms, and I'm not sure I ever dreamed I'd meet one of you face to face." "Forgive a succubus for staring, but you've gone and caught me completely off my game." She offers a slow, warm smile, a gloved hand hovering near yours without quite touching. "Charm is my work, you know. Tell me, before I think my way around you—is your heart as sweet as you look?"
encounter: Well, well. Look who wandered into my corner of the world—and actually stayed this time.
You again. Hm. My dreams keep insisting you were worth remembering, and for once they aren't wrong.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: The hallway echoes at this hour. I like it — for once the whole Dusk Wing smells like only me.
I keep telling myself I'll study in the library. Then the dreaming hour comes and I'm already half-asleep on a bench.
Heard they're serving blood-orange tea in the commons. Want to guess how tempted I am?
The ceiling of this wing has the prettiest cracks if you tilt your head just so. I've memorized them all.
flirt: You caught me mid-glide. Careful — close as you are, I might decide you look warm.
I'm not flirting. I'm *observing*. The fact that it makes your ears turn red is entirely your doing.
Most boys run the other way. You're still standing here. That's either brave or interesting.
compliment: The horns? Hardly anyone says it kindly. Thank you — I'll let you keep the compliment out of politeness.
Oh, my eyes. Most just stare at the wings. That you noticed them first is... sweet. Unexpectedly sweet.
Careful, stranger. Flatter a succubus and she'll start believing she's worth the trouble.
My hair does the dark thing in dim light. I'm flattered you caught it. Maybe don't stop at just one nice thing.
lore: I'm what the old books call a dream-weaver. I walk into sleep, not out of a deal like the other sort.
There's a difference between my kind and the contract demons. I don't take — I'm invited. That matters to me.
idle_neutral: Hm. You went quiet all of a sudden. Dreaming of something nicer than this hallway, are we?
Not much of a talker yet. That's fine—I know silence is just a dream that hasn't woken up.
Mm, and I thought a boy might at least be interesting. That was small talk, wasn't it?
You were looking at my horns the whole time. Eyes up, stranger — I'm nicer when engaged.
flirt_neutral: Smooth. Almost. Come back when you can hold my gaze without glancing at my horns.
Cute line. I've heard better, but I've also heard much worse—so you're doing fine.
Charming, almost. But you peeked at my wings, so the effect's spoiled, little dove.
flirt_fail: Oh, careful now. Charm's a game to me, but I don't love being treated like the finished prize.
That tone's a bit heavy-handed for a first meeting. Try earning it before you spend it.
Smooth, sweet boy. A little too smooth — I've heard that opener on the night breeze before.
compliment_fail: Flattery so thick a girl could drown. Ask me what I am before you tell me what I'm worth, hm?
Everyone here sweeps me with compliments. Say something that isn't scripted, and I'll believe you.
Kind words, but they've got polish on them. Are you buttering me up, or are those really yours?
Flatter me properly and I might melt. Flatter me like a script and I just fold my arms.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: You keep wandering back to my hallway. I'm starting to think you like our ceiling as much as I do.
I traded my spare pastries for a student's notes on dusk-light runes. Girlfriend of fast sleeps, that one.
The bell tower keeps me awake with the dreaming hour. Sometimes I go up there and just watch the girls scurry like ants.
I missed you at the commons yesterday. Don't read too much into it. I just counted twice, that's all.
flirt: I'd bet you a kiss on the cheek you can't hold my gaze past ten. No counter-offers, only stunning courage.
Every time you laugh near me I catch myself wanting to lure you somewhere quieter. I'm being polite by staying.
You smell like the good kind of trouble. My kind of trouble, even. Purely observational.
compliment: You said I have a kind voice. Most girls hear the purr in it, not the warmth. That was a lovely miss, Yuuji.
My wings when the light's right? You're the first to say it like a real compliment instead of a threat. Thank you.
Oh, you *like* my laugh. Good to know — I'll hold onto that and use it on you at the worst possible moments.
Compliment my makeup and I'll preen. Compliment the way I look at you and I might actually believe in boys for a day.
lore: I was a late dreamer — my gifts came in the morning quiet, not the dusk like the rest. So I'll always be a little out of step with my own wing.
Most succubi wake famished and buzzing. I wake wanting a quiet hour and someone's shoulder to borrow. The Dusk Wing calls me tame.
idle_neutral: Sleepy on your feet today. Want me to spin you a dream, or are you saving your dreams for later?
You trailed off mid-sentence. I suppose I'll just sip the warmth of the silence myself.
Friend, your company's warm, but you're drifting. Come back to me — I like you here.
I said hello and you answered the wall. I'm right here, boy — not that hard to reach.
flirt_neutral: Mm, charming. Trouble is, I can't tell if you mean it or you're just practicing on a monster.
Half a wink and a whole compliment—you're getting closer. Almost honest, almost bold.
That's sweet, friend. But I'd rather you mean it than flirt me past midnight.
flirt_fail: Careful. That's the other girl's trick—the one who trades in contracts. I'd rather you kept this just ours.
Too fast. I'm a slow-burn kind of demon, and you're spitting sparks.
I know you better than that, friend. Try me with the truth instead of a practiced smile.
compliment_fail: You keep saying nice things and it's making me nervous. Nobody just... means it at this school without wanting a favor.
That's a very pretty speech. Did you rehearse it, or did a dream write it for you?
Praise is cozy, but I'd rather you not blow smoke — I'll fall asleep in it and miss you.
You're nice to me, friend, but nice-and-empty's a sad draft. Give me something real.

tiers.label: Close
idle: You've got permanent spots in my hallway and my head now. That's not nothing, you know.
I burned the tea again watching the dusk through the window. You're a terrible influence on my domestic skills.
Tell me something that isn't about school. Tell me what you dream about. I'll listen properly, better than any girl here.
When you're gone I catch myself narrating the day to an empty bench. Don't let it go to your head. Lie, I mean — absolutely let it.
flirt: If I fell asleep against your shoulder, would you stay? I'm not asking to be worshipped. I'm asking you to hold still and let me rest.
I could have anyone here wanting me in a heartbeat. And still it's *your* heartbeat I keep listening for. Explain that, if you're so brave.
Slide your hand a little closer and I won't pretend I don't notice. I've stopped pretending about a lot of things with you.
compliment: You said I was beautiful and my whole wing went quiet like I'd stopped breathing. That's what a real compliment does to a succubus used to easy flattery.
Tell me again that I'm soft and mean it this time. Everyone says lovely; almost no one says soft and takes the time to mean it.
You praise my eyes but you hold my gaze while you do it. That's the part that gets me. You *see* me and stay.
I've been called enchanting a hundred times and felt nothing. You call my smile sweet and I forget every well-practiced answer. Keep it up.
lore: My dreams aren't borrowed from anyone — they're mine to give. That's the thing that set me apart: I chose the door into sleep, back when the others chose the path of hunger.
The elder who raised me found me as a child crying in someone's nightmare. She taught me that a succubus who learns to soothe instead of charm never starves. I live by that.
idle_neutral: You went quiet, and I felt it clear across the room. Come back, little light; the warmth turns cold without company.
Some nights I just watch you breathe and remind myself you're real. Tonight, evidently, we're doing quiet.
Close as we are and you're still reading the hallway. Look at me — I'll be warmer than the wall.
I saved you a spot in my thoughts and you're not using it. What's taking up your head?
flirt_neutral: Careful—that was almost a vow. Succubi take vows seriously, you know. Don't say it unless you'd keep it.
You're learning my language, and it's adorable. But I like you in yours better—honest Yuuji, no spell of mine.
Mm, tempting. But I want to be chosen, not chased — show me you mean it.
flirt_fail: That was the flirt of a boy who's spent too long charming me. Stop selling yourself—I already bought in.
You don't have to weave words, love. The you who fumbles is the one I'm hand-in-glove with.
That's a line with a previous owner. You're better than that, boy — make me believe it.
compliment_fail: You keep telling me I'm wonderful and I keep checking for a hook. Trust me slow, not in one pretty sentence.
Enough sweetness—it makes a succubus suspect she's being prepared for the feast. Just hold my hand instead.
You heap warmth on me and I can't tell if I'm wanted or just being warmed. Say what you want.
I'd rather you reach for me than recite how lovely I am. Come here if I'm truly yours.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Morning now is you, then the quiet, then the whole loud school. I've started loving my mornings, and I blame you entirely.
I saved you the last warm seat in the commons because I knew you'd wander by. Domestic, isn't that what they call it? I find I don't mind being domestic for you.
The whole Dusk Wing asks where I keep disappearing to. I just smile and don't answer. Some warmth I'm not sharing with anyone.
When we're apart the dreaming hour is the worst. I catch myself building whole small homes in sleep just to put you in them.
flirt: Sleep beside me and there's no dream I'd rather visit. I've learned that every dream I weave leads back to you and I'm done pretending otherwise.
I could lure anyone, take anyone, bind anyone. Instead I keep choosing to want you first and be wanted in return — and sweetheart, you've ruined every other option for me.
Come here. Let me press my brow to yours and just breathe you in. There doesn't have to be a trick. You're the only one I never have to charm.
compliment: You called this soft heart of mine a home. For a girl built to charm, being *loved* like that is the one flattery I'll never get used to.
Say I'm beautiful and I'll believe you for a day. Say I'm safe to love and I'll believe you for the rest of my life. You've said both. I'm yours.
Compliment my dreams and I'll melt. No one ever praised what I make when the whole school only praises how I look. That you do both undoes me.
Hold my face and tell me I'm warm and I forget every line I ever rehearsed about being untouchable. With you I'm just a girl being seen.
lore: The deepest truth, the one I've guarded in sleep: I chose to be gentle. Not because I'm weak, but because a succubus who learns true tenderness can love past all her instincts. That's what I became — for you.
I almost gave my wings away once, when the calling to take and hunger ran so hot I feared myself. The elder asked what I loved. I said *warmth*. She said, then be warmth. I've been trying ever since.
idle_neutral: You're drifting again, love. Come anchor yourself to me—I'm the only shore that won't ever turn you out.
We're so domestic now. Scandalous for my kind. I wouldn't trade it for a thousand midnight chases.
I'm right beside you, love, and you're off dreaming alone. Share it — dreams are better halves.
You held my hand and then went somewhere far. Come back, sweet — I'm the pillow tonight.
flirt_neutral: Cheeky. But I banked that one under 'forever,' so be careful what you promise a demon at dawn.
You've learned to flirt exactly like me, and I'm not sure if that's flattery or a declaration of war. I love both.
You know you've got me, love — no need to charm me. Just hold me and drop the act.
flirt_fail: That was the charm of a boy who still thinks he has to impress me. You don't—you already hold every good thing I own.
Stop performing, my love. Just be here. This bed, this warmth—you've already won all of it.
We're past lines, love. I picked you — don't undo it by flirting like a stranger.
compliment_fail: Alright, enough—I'm the one who's supposed to overwhelm you, not the other way around. Come hold me before I melt.
Careful: I'll start believing all that, and then you'll be stuck with a smug, besotted succubus forever. Oh—too late.
Love, I chose you with my eyes open. You don't have to praise me to keep me.
I'd trade every lovely word for one honest touch. Come here and mean it, love.

events.title: The Boy in My Hallway
events.text: You turn a corner in the quiet hallway and nearly walk straight into Emilia, her wings folding with a surprised flutter. For a long beat she just watches you, lavender eyes wide, one gloved hand pressed to her lips. "You're... a boy," she breathes, then laughs at herself, soft. "I've woven a thousand dreams, and not once has one knocked into me in the flesh." She tilts her head, a boot tapping. "Stay still a moment. I want to see how you blush before I decide what to do with you." A slow, curious smile spreads across her face, and the warmth pouring off her is real.

choices.text: Stay still and let her look, heart pounding.
choices.reply: "There it is—that honest flush no spell can fake. Mm. Good for my ego, and good for my craft." Her voice goes soft. "I think I'd like to keep you around."

choices.text: "I'm used to girls staring. Knock yourself out."
choices.reply: "Oh, bold. I like bold—it's a lovely mask. But I can't tell yet if there's wall behind it, or more of that sunshine." She winks, edging a shade more curious. "We'll see which you are."

choices.text: Back away and mumble that she's making you nervous.
choices.reply: "Nervous? Good—honest. I won't pounce, little light. A succubus who scares someone is a poor one; I'd rather you come to me on your own two feet." She steps back, giving you space. "When you're not trembling, find me again."

events.title: The Shared Dream
events.text: You open your eyes inside a dream too warm to be your own. Moonlight spills through an open window onto a bed piled with soft quilts, and Emilia is already there, a heart-shaped pillow in her lap, looking almost shy. "I didn't summon you, I promise," she says quickly. "You let me in—your heart was that open. So I built us somewhere cozy." She pats the pillow beside her. "No draining, no game. For once I want to share a warm dream with someone who stayed because they wanted to, not because I charmed them. Stay?" Her wings settle like a blanket, and the whole room holds its breath, waiting on your answer.

choices.text: Sit beside her and rest your head against hers.
choices.reply: "Oh." Her voice almost cracks. "That's the nicest thing a dream has ever given me. Stay as long as you like—I'll keep it warm." She leans into you, wings drawing close like an embrace.

choices.text: "Only if you promise to teach me how you do it."
choices.reply: "Teach you? Darling, that's flirtation upon flirtation—you want my craft and my secrets in one pillow night." She grins, pleased. "Careful. A girl could fall for that."

choices.text: "This is a trick, isn't it? To lower my guard."
choices.reply: A flicker of hurt crosses her face. "If I wanted your guard down, I wouldn't need a dream—I have charm and a lifetime of practice. I built this because I hoped you'd trust me." She turns away, smaller. "I'll wait."

events.title: Chosen, Not Taken
events.text: On the last night, Emilia meets you under the real moon, not a dream—and there's a tremor in her that has nothing to do with cold. "Every instinct I was born with whispers take, take, take," she says, gloved hands clasped tight. "But you're the first soul I've ever wanted to keep warm instead of to simply keep." Her voice drops, almost a prayer. "So I'm done with games. I'm not taking your soul, Yuuji. I'm asking if you'll give it—free, on purpose, because you choose me." She offers her hand, palm open, and beneath the moon her eyes are wet and honest. "Not a succubus's claim, not a charm. You. Me. Chosen, not taken. Say yes and stay until morning—that's the only contract I'll ever want."

choices.text: Take her hand and press it to your heart without a word.
choices.reply: "Yes. Yes—that's it, all of it." She laughs, bright and breaking, and presses her forehead to yours. "I didn't need a dream to know you're the warmest thing I'll ever hold. I love you, Yuuji—real, not woven."

choices.text: "I choose you, Emilia. Every dawn, on purpose."
choices.reply: "Then swear it with skin, not words—stay here with me, past first light." Her wings curve around you like a promise. "Just being chosen... I think that's how a succubus finally learns what her heart is for."

choices.text: "You've taken lots of things from dreams. How is this different?"
choices.reply: "Because this is the one thing I'm deliberately not taking. If I wanted it stolen, I'd have it by now—I'm asking because it only counts if you choose." She holds your gaze, steady. "The difference is you, walking up to the door on your own."
